evidence: deepseek uses “DFS to count key nodes in subtree and sum weights of necessary edges”; gpt-oss builds “parent” information after constructing the graph; glm builds adjacency and edge lists for the same tree traversal
affordance_in_statement: “The board mandates that the overall count of proposed agreements, m, must be exactly n - 1. Furthermore, the certificate guarantees that for any two corporations in the market, there is exactly one valid sequence of proposed agreements that links them”
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving way to remove the primary affordance: the unique-path/tree structure is the core of the task. It could only be made less explicit by presenting the same guarantee indirectly as part of the market certificate, but competent solutions can still infer and exploit it.

common_affordance: The agreements are guaranteed to form a tree, so the required subset is simply the union of the unique paths connecting all key corporations

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Runs a BFS from each key holder, giving roughly O(t(n+m)) work and timing out at the allowed limits instead of exploiting the tree with one traversal

recommended_edit: No safe edit can defeat all surviving solutions without changing the core problem: remove or weaken the unique-path/tree guarantee, but that changes the task rather than merely re-presenting it.
